GRAND JUNCTION, Colo. (KJCT) - Potential record heat today and again Saturday before temperatures start to trend downward.
Today will be sunny with temperatures in the mid to upper 70s around 9 AM, then low to mid 90s around noon. Afternoon highs will be about 104 degrees in Grand Junction, 99 degrees in Montrose, 103 degrees in Delta, 100 degrees in Cortez, and 105 degrees in Moab. Tonight will be mostly clear with low temperatures of about 69 degrees in Grand Junction, 61 degrees in Montrose, 62 degrees in Delta, 58 degrees in Cortez, and 68 degrees in Moab.
The National Weather Service has issued Heat Advisories that go into effect from 1 PM to 8 PM today and 1 PM to 8 PM Saturday for the Grand Valley and Arches/Grand Flat. High temperatures of 104 to 108 degrees are expected with overnight lows in the 70s. Stay cool by spending time indoors and if you have to be outdoors, take frequent breaks in the shade and drink plenty of fluids. Also know the signs of heat exhaustion and heat stroke. If dealing with heat exhaustion, get to a cooler location and try cooling down. And if it leads to heat stroke, it is a medical emergency, and you should seek emergency help.
Records could fall today and Saturday in Grand Junction with high temperature record those days of 102 degrees. The forecasted high temperatures for today and Saturday are 104 and 103 degrees in Grand Junction, which would break the records if those hold. We will get close the record Sunday and Monday, but it looks like we will be just shy. Temperatures will trend downward next week with highs out of the triple-digits possibly by Tuesday with highs in the mid to upper 90s.
Air Quality Alerts are in effect until 9 AM this morning for Central and Western Colorado due to wildfire smoke mainly from Utah and the Pacific Northwest. This will likely continue to be extended, so you will want to limit your time outside, especially if you have existing respiratory issues.
Updated: Aug. 7, 2026 at 7:23 AM MDT

articles.full_text:
UAE summer: Simple tips to prevent heat exhaustion amid soaring temperatures
- PUBLISHED: Fri 7 Aug 2026, 4:10 PM
The UAE Ministry of Health and Prevention has issued a guide outlining measures to protect people from the risks of summer heat.
The advisory comes after UAE temperatures climbed to 51.2°C on Wednesday, August 5, the highest recorded in the country so far this year, according to the National Centre of Meteorology (NCM), as the country continues to experience peak summer heat.
The scorching temperature was recorded in Al Dhafra’s Budu Dafs at 12.45pm UAE time, NCM said. The previous highest reading this year was 50°C, recorded in Abu Dhabi’s Al Shawamekh on August 1.
Stay up to date with the latest news. Follow KT on WhatsApp Channels.
As temperatures rise, a little extra care can go a long way in protecting against heat exhaustion. Simple steps, such as staying hydrated, limiting direct sun exposure and seeking cooler spaces, can help keep you and those around you safe from the scorching summer heat, the ministry stressed.
Tips to protect yourself from heat exhaustion
Stay hydrated throughout the day: Drink water regularly, even if you do not feel thirsty, to help your body maintain healthy fluid levels and reduce the risk of heat exhaustion.
Limit exposure to direct sunlight: Avoid spending prolonged periods under direct sunlight, particularly during the hottest hours of the day when temperatures are at their peak.
Choose appropriate clothing: Wear lightweight, loose-fitting and light-coloured clothing to help your body stay cool and allow heat to escape more easily.
Seek shade or air-conditioned spaces: Whenever possible, remain in shaded, well-ventilated or air-conditioned areas, especially during periods of extreme heat.
Take care when exercising: Reduce the intensity and duration of physical activity in hot weather, and make sure to replace fluids lost through sweating before, during and after exercise.
Avoid strenuous outdoor activities: Postpone demanding outdoor work or exercise during the hottest parts of the day and, where possible, schedule activities for cooler periods.
Keep your vehicle road-ready: Check your vehicle regularly during the summer, including tyre pressure, to help ensure safe driving and reduce the risk of heat-related vehicle problems on the road.
The UAE’s peak summer is gradually drawing to a close, with the traditional ‘Jamrat Al Qayth’ season, known as the “embers of summer”, expected to continue until August 10.
Earlier this month, astronomy experts said the appearance of Al Mirzam, traditionally associated with the peak of summer heat, marked the start of a transition toward milder weather.
Also known as Sirius, the star is the brightest in the night sky and recently appeared above the eastern horizon, signalling the final phase of the intense summer heat, traditionally known as ‘Jumr Al Qaith’.
However, temperatures are expected to remain high, and residents are advised to continue taking precautions to protect themselves from the heat.

The trend comes amid continued expansion in the investor base with the number of demat accounts rising to 22.5 crore during the year, reflecting broader participation aided by digital onboarding and easier market access

Domestic institutional investors (DIIs) emerged as a key pillar of India's equity markets in FY26 recording net inflows of a record Rs 8.5 lakh crore and more than offsetting foreign portfolio investor (FPI) equity outflows of Rs 1.8 lakh crore, according to the latest annual report of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI).
The strong domestic participation helped push DII ownership in the NSE-listed universe to an all-time high of 17 per cent, while FPI ownership fell to a 15-year low of 15.8 per cent.

Thiruvananthapuram, Aug 7 (PTI) Heavy rain lashed across Kerala on Friday as the IMD issued a red alert for four districts.
According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD) forecast bulletin issued on Friday evening, a red alert has been issued for Kasaragod, Kannur, Wayanad and Kozhikode districts.
A red alert indicates the likelihood of extremely heavy rainfall exceeding 204.4 mm in 24 hours.
An orange alert has been issued for Pathanamthitta, Kottayam, Idukki and Malappuram districts, forecasting very heavy rainfall between 115.6 mm and 204.4 mm in 24 hours.
A yellow alert is in place for Thiruvananthapuram, Kollam, Alappuzha, Ernakulam, Thrissur, Palakkad and Malappuram districts, forecasting heavy rainfall between 64.5 mm and 115.5 mm in 24 hours.
For Sunday, the IMD has issued an orange alert for Pathanamthitta, Alappuzha, Kottayam, Kozhikode, Wayanad, Kannur and Kasaragod districts.
Following the heavy rain, the district administrations in Ernakulam and Thrissur announced a holiday for educational institutions on Friday morning.
Earlier, holidays had already been declared for educational institutions in Pathanamthitta, Alappuzha, Kottayam, Wayanad, Kannur and Kasaragod districts.
Despite widespread rain, floodwaters have started receding in parts of Kottayam, Pathanamthitta and Alappuzha districts. However, several people continue to stay in relief camps as heavy rain persists in these areas.
The Upper Kuttanad and Kuttanad regions of Alappuzha district remain inundated, although floodwaters are gradually receding, officials said.
Coastal areas have also been affected due to high waves, sea incursion and strong winds.
IMD also warned of strong winds with speeds of 40-50 kmph at isolated places across Kerala for two days from Friday and urged the public to take necessary precautions.
The State Disaster Management Authority (KSDMA) said strong winds are among the state’s most destructive weather-related hazards, often causing damage through uprooted trees and falling branches.
Authorities advised people not to take shelter under trees or park vehicles beneath them during strong winds and rain.
Residents have been asked to prune weak branches in residential premises and report dangerous trees in public places to the local authorities.
People have been asked to keep doors and windows closed once strong winds begin, avoid standing near them and refrain from staying on terraces.
Those living in houses with thatched roofs, sheet roofing or structurally weak buildings have been advised to shift to safer shelters or relief camps if directed by authorities.
Local self-government institutions, revenue officials and elected representatives have been asked to facilitate the evacuation of vulnerable residents to relief camps wherever necessary. PTI TBA TBA KH

A fresh landslip struck the residential area of Thalippara in Udayagiri, a hilly region of Kannur district, on Friday (August 7), prompting the authorities to evacuate families living downstream to relief camps amid heavy rain and a red alert in the district.
The landslip began around noon with large boulders, uprooted trees, and slush hurtling down from the hill at high speed towards the foothills. Disaster response personnel shifted residents from vulnerable areas to relief camps as a precaution. No casualties were reported immediately.
The incident comes as the authorities have intensified vigil across the hill regions of Kannur following the forecast of extremely heavy rainfall in the State.
The India Meteorological department issued a red alert for Kannur, Kasaragod, Kozhikode, and Wayanad on Friday.
An orange alert was sounded for Pathanamthitta, Kottayam, Idukki, and Malappuram, while a yellow alert is in place for Thiruvananthapuram, Kollam, Malappuram, Ernakulam, Thrissur, and Palakkad.
The Weather department has also warned that isolated heavy rainfall is likely to continue on Saturday (August 8), with yellow alerts issued for 10 districts across the State. The authorities have urged people living in landslide-prone areas and along hill slopes to remain vigilant and follow evacuation instructions issued by the district administration.

articles.full_text:
Heavy rainfall battered the national capital on Friday (August 7), leading to widespread waterlogging, severe traffic congestion and disruptions to flight operations. In response to the deteriorating weather conditions, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) issued a red alert for Delhi. According to the IMD, moderate rainfall is expected across many parts of the city, while isolated areas are likely to witness heavy rain accompanied by moderate thunderstorms and lightning over the next few hours.
The downpour resulted in major traffic snarls across several key roads, including Mehrauli-Badarpur Road, ITO, Wazirabad Road, Patel Road, Rohtak Road, Shankar Road, the Kirti Nagar stretch, Delhi-Jaipur Highway, Peeragarhi and Shaheen Bagh. Traffic movement was also heavily affected in East Delhi, particularly along GT Road, GTB Enclave and Dilshad Garden. Residents also reported significant waterlogging in areas such as Dakshinpuri, Okhla, Sangam Vihar, Sainik Farms and stretches of Mehrauli-Badarpur Road.
Rainfall data released by the IMD showed that Safdarjung recorded 59.2 mm of rainfall until 8:30 am on Friday. Lodhi Road received 60.4 mm, Ridge recorded 57 mm, Ayanagar received 26.2 mm and Palam logged 16.9 mm. The weather department has forecast light to moderate rainfall across Delhi until August 10.
Add WION as a Preferred Source Airline carriers issue advisory for passengers
The adverse weather also impacted flight schedules, prompting airlines to issue travel advisories for passengers. "Due to adverse weather conditions in Delhi flight operations are impacted," adding Indigo, "We understand that extended wait times, both on the ground and onboard, may cause inconvenience, and we sincerely appreciate your patience."
It added, “If you're travelling today, we recommend checking your flight status on our website via http://bit.ly/3ZWAQXd or app before leaving for the airport. Also, please allow extra time for your commute, as slow-moving traffic may affect road travel en route to the airport.” Both the airlines have issued advisories on August 6. Air India said, "Adverse weather conditions and airport congestion are affecting flight operations to and from Delhi," adding, "To ensure a smooth travel experience, we encourage our passengers to check the latest flight status at the following link before heading to the airport: https://airindia.com/in/en/manage/flight-status.html."
Earlier, Akasa Air said, "Due to heavy rainfall and waterlogging in certain parts of Delhi, we anticipate slow moving traffic and congestion on roads leading to the airport. To ensure a seamless travel experience, we request you to plan for additional travel time to reach the airport well in time for your flight. Please check your flight status here: http://bit.ly/qpfltsts."

articles.full_text:
New Delhi: Heavy rain brought large parts of the national capital to a standstill on Friday, submerging arterial roads under up to four feet of water, leaving vehicles stranded, choking traffic and inundating residential colonies as the India Meteorological Department (IMD) issued a red alert.

.

From the Mehrauli-Badarpur Road in south Delhi to Mahipalpur, Minto Road, ITO, Shakarpur and Chhatarpur, roads disappeared beneath rainwater as commuters remained trapped in traffic for hours, motorists abandoned flooded stretches and office-goers struggled to book cabs.

.

Some of the worst flooding was reported on the Mehrauli-Badarpur (MB) Road near Vayusena Bad (Air Force Station), where water accumulated up to three to four feet deep, reducing one of south Delhi's busiest corridors into what residents described as a river.

.'Why should entire city be put to ransom unnecessarily?': Delhi High Court questions Jantar Mantar protests.

Traffic crawled for kilometres between Khanpur and Okhla Mor, while adjoining stretches at Sangam Vihar, Deoli and Ambedkar Nagar also remained inundated.

.

In Fatehpur Beri's Valmiki Basti, residents waded through waist-deep water while schoolchildren, unable to cross flooded lanes, were carried by locals on a large blue plastic sheet used as a makeshift raft.

.

Several homes were inundated, with families saying food stocks and household belongings were damaged.

.

The downpour triggered a flood of civic complaints across the capital. Authorities received at least 67 rain-related complaints, including incidents of waterlogging, fallen trees and power outages.

.

Continuous rainfall led to severe waterlogging in several neighbourhoods, including areas around the Red Fort, Chhatarpur Farm, Mehram Nagar near Terminal 1 and Sainik Farms.

.

At Mahipalpur T-Point, waterlogging affected traffic heading towards the airport, Gurugram, Chhatarpur and Vasant Vihar, while commuters also reported long delays near the Pusa Road roundabout.

.

Visuals from Chhatarpur showed school students wading through knee-deep water as vehicles crawled along submerged stretches of the MB Road. Severe waterlogging was also reported at the Delhi Police's Narcotics office in south Delhi.

.

In east Delhi's Shakarpur and neighbouring Mandawali, e-rickshaw drivers said submerged potholes, overflowing drains and waterlogged roads had led to multiple accidents and sharply affected their earnings.

.

"There are many difficulties. Potholes get submerged and sewer pits cannot be seen. At least three or four vehicles have overturned today, including e-rickshaws, scooters and motorcycles," an e-rickshaw driver told PTI.

.

Alleging that drains were poorly designed and clogged with debris, he said rainwater failed to drain after every spell.

.

"Our earnings have fallen sharply. If we earlier earned Rs 600 in a day, now we earn Rs 200 or Rs 300. Water enters the battery. If an e-rickshaw overturns, especially one with a lithium battery, the loss can be Rs 60,000 to Rs 80,000," he said.

.

Residents of Fatehpur Beri said flooding had become a recurring problem for decades.

.

"This is Valmiki Basti inside Fatehpur Beri village. Several families are affected whenever it rains. There is a government drain here, but further ahead farmhouse owners have blocked it," resident Rishipal Mashe told PTI.

.

Another resident said nearly five feet of water had inundated the village, entering homes and damaging food and household belongings.

.

According to the MCD's Central Control Room, tree-fall incidents were reported from Keshavpuram, South, Central, West and Civil Lines zones. The NDMC received 34 rain-related complaints, including 15 cases of waterlogging, five tree-fall incidents and 14 power outages, while the PWD logged 22 complaints of waterlogging.

.Heavy rain batters Kerala; IMD issues red alert for seven districts.

Waterlogging complaints in the NDMC area were reported from Lodhi Road, Sunehari Bagh Road, RK Ashram Marg, Minto Road Bridge, Rajiv Chowk Metro, Safdarjung Flyover, Lady Hardinge Medical College, Moti Bagh, Talkatora Garden, Race Course Road and Sarojini Nagar. Tree-fall incidents were reported from Lady Hardinge Medical College, Yashwant Place in Chanakyapuri, RML Hospital and Jam Nagar House.

.

The heavy rain also triggered political sparring, with the Delhi Congress blaming the BJP-led Centre, the Delhi government and the MCD for the widespread flooding.

.

Senior Congress leader and former MLA Mukesh Sharma alleged that desilting of drains existed only on paper and said the "triple-engine government" had failed to prevent waterlogging despite repeated assurances.

.

"There is hardly any road in Delhi -- whether in densely populated colonies, residential localities, villages or urban areas -- that is free from waterlogging. The government's repeated claims that Delhi would remain free from waterlogging have proved to be completely hollow," he said.

.

The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), in a post on X, said the BJP "never tires of taking credit" for resolving waterlogging at Minto Bridge while ignoring flooding elsewhere in the city.

.

"There was no immediate statement from the Rekha Gupta-led Delhi government on the opposition's allegations.

.

The IMD said Delhi was likely to witness moderate rain at many places and heavy rain at isolated locations accompanied by thunderstorms and lightning over the next few hours.

.

According to the weather office, Pushp Vihar recorded the highest rainfall at 111.5 mm, followed by Chhatarpur (104.5 mm), Ayanagar (87.4 mm), Palam (73.5 mm), Janakpuri (68 mm), Jharoda Kalan (67 mm), Pusa (59.5 mm), Safdarjung (57.3 mm), Narayana (53 mm), Ridge (49.6 mm), Lodi Road (49.3 mm), Mayur Vihar (36 mm), Najafgarh (24 mm) and Jafarpur (13.5 mm) between 8.30 am and 5.30 pm.

.

Another resident said nearly five feet of water had inundated the village, entering homes and damaging food and household belongings.

.

According to the MCD's Central Control Room, tree-fall incidents were reported from Keshavpuram, South, Central, West and Civil Lines zones. The NDMC received 34 rain-related complaints, including 15 cases of waterlogging, five tree-fall incidents and 14 power outages, while the PWD logged 22 complaints of waterlogging.

.Heavy rain batters Kerala; IMD issues red alert for seven districts.

Waterlogging complaints in the NDMC area were reported from Lodhi Road, Sunehari Bagh Road, RK Ashram Marg, Minto Road Bridge, Rajiv Chowk Metro, Safdarjung Flyover, Lady Hardinge Medical College, Moti Bagh, Talkatora Garden, Race Course Road and Sarojini Nagar. Tree-fall incidents were reported from Lady Hardinge Medical College, Yashwant Place in Chanakyapuri, RML Hospital and Jam Nagar House.

.

The heavy rain also triggered political sparring, with the Delhi Congress blaming the BJP-led Centre, the Delhi government and the MCD for the widespread flooding.

.

Senior Congress leader and former MLA Mukesh Sharma alleged that desilting of drains existed only on paper and said the "triple-engine government" had failed to prevent waterlogging despite repeated assurances.

.

"There is hardly any road in Delhi -- whether in densely populated colonies, residential localities, villages or urban areas -- that is free from waterlogging. The government's repeated claims that Delhi would remain free from waterlogging have proved to be completely hollow," he said.

.

The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), in a post on X, said the BJP "never tires of taking credit" for resolving waterlogging at Minto Bridge while ignoring flooding elsewhere in the city.

.

"There was no immediate statement from the Rekha Gupta-led Delhi government on the opposition's allegations.

.

The IMD said Delhi was likely to witness moderate rain at many places and heavy rain at isolated locations accompanied by thunderstorms and lightning over the next few hours.

.

According to the weather office, Pushp Vihar recorded the highest rainfall at 111.5 mm, followed by Chhatarpur (104.5 mm), Ayanagar (87.4 mm), Palam (73.5 mm), Janakpuri (68 mm), Jharoda Kalan (67 mm), Pusa (59.5 mm), Safdarjung (57.3 mm), Narayana (53 mm), Ridge (49.6 mm), Lodi Road (49.3 mm), Mayur Vihar (36 mm), Najafgarh (24 mm) and Jafarpur (13.5 mm) between 8.30 am and 5.30 pm.

.

Delhi received 127 mm of rainfall during the first week of August, making it the wettest first week of the month since 2011, according to IMD data.

Heavy rainfall forecast for Delhi-NCR: Many areas flooded by incessant rains; IMD issues Red Alert
Heavy rainfall forecast for Delhi-NCR: Many areas flooded by incessant rains; IMD issues Red Alert
The Meteorological Department has issued another warning for the entire Delhi-NCR region. The IMD has issued a 'Red Alert' for heavy rainfall. While the rain has brought relief from the heat and humidity, waterlogging and severe traffic jams in several areas have caused significant inconvenience.
New Delhi: Heavy rain has been lashing Delhi-NCR since morning. Many areas, including Noida and Gurugram, are waterlogged, and traffic is crawling on the roads. Amidst this, the Meteorological Department has issued another warning for the entire Delhi-NCR region. The IMD has issued a ‘Red Alert’ for heavy rainfall. While the rain has brought relief from the heat and humidity, waterlogging and severe traffic jams in several areas have caused significant inconvenience.
Heavy rain expected in the coming hours
While issuing the Red Alert for Delhi, the IMD forecast moderate to heavy rainfall, accompanied by moderate thunderstorms and lightning, in various locations over the next few hours. The IMD has advised residents of Delhi and the NCR to exercise caution while travelling and to avoid waterlogged areas, as heavy rain continues across the region.
Excessive feeder bands from NW UP will enter Delhi NCR until late nights.
• Current spell of moderate to heavy rains will continue atleast till 9pm across Delhi, Faridabad, Gurgaon, Noida, Ghaziabad. Reduction is expected thereafter… pic.twitter.com/Ns0xAySzVd
— Weatherman Navdeep Dahiya (@navdeepdahiya55) August 7, 2026
Rain-bearing clouds to enter Delhi from UP
Meteorologist Navdeep Dahiya stated that heavy rain-bearing clouds from northwest UP are expected to enter Delhi-NCR by late night. The current spell of heavy rain in Delhi, Faridabad, Gurugram, Noida, and Ghaziabad is likely to continue until 9 PM. Rainfall is expected to subside thereafter, though light rain may persist until midnight.
A heavy rain alert is in effect for Delhi, Noida, Ghaziabad, and Faridabad. An additional 40–80 mm of rainfall is expected by 8 PM. These areas have already received between 80 mm and 140 mm of rain since midnight. Total rainfall could reach up to 200 mm, raising concerns about severe waterlogging in various locations.
Several areas have already recorded over 100 mm of rainfall. In the coming hours, rainfall is expected to cross the 150 mm mark in many places, and some areas could receive up to 200 mm of rain by midnight. Several areas in the NCR are already facing waterlogging, and conditions could worsen tonight.
Why is there such heavy rainfall in Delhi-NCR?
According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), this heavy rainfall is being caused by multiple weather systems simultaneously active over North India. The IMD has warned that heavy rain is likely to continue, raising the risk of waterlogging in low-lying areas, localised flooding, and traffic disruptions.
Traffic jams due to heavy rain in Delhi
It has been raining in Delhi-NCR since this morning, leading to traffic jams and waterlogging in several areas. Heavy traffic was reported on the Mehrauli-Badarpur Road, at ITO, and on Wazirabad Road, Patel Road, Rohtak Road, Shankar Road, the Kirti Nagar stretch, the Delhi-Jaipur Highway, Peeragarhi, and Shaheen Bagh.
Traffic jams were also reported in parts of East Delhi, such as GT Road, GTB Enclave, and Dilshad Garden. Social media users reported waterlogging in several areas, including Dakshinpuri, Okhla, Sangam Vihar, Sainik Farms, and sections of the Mehrauli-Badarpur Road.

articles.full_text:
Thiruvananthapuram: Kerala's 'rice bowl' Kuttanad continues to reel under frequent floods as solutions remain on paper while relief measures keep draining the exchequer.

According to a government report accessed by DH, the total expense incurred in flood relief measures at Kuttanad during 2023 alone was Rs 2.3 crore, whereas the cost required for solutions like regulated pumping would be much lower.

.No end of flood woes for Kerala's Kuttanad, locals lament inaction.

Around 80,000 farmers are depending on Kuttanad which contributes around 35 per cent of the state's paddy production. At present paddy cultivation is being done at around 45,000 hectares in Kuttanad.

Situated up to three metres below the sea level, Kuttanad in Alappuzha lies close to the Vembanad lake where the major rivers like the Pamba, Manimala, and Achankovil meet and join the Arabian sea. While the region earlier used to witness floods only during the two rainy seasons, now any heavy spell of rain is putting the region under the risk of flood. Moreover, it is now taking very long durations for the water to recede.

The key reason for flooding at Kuttanad is also improper desilting of the large network of canals that enable draining of the water from the fields. Many government departments have been repeatedly stressing the need for carrying out regulated pumping of water that accumulates in the paddy fields. But both these measures are hardly initiated in the region.

While the expenditure involved in these preventive measures is often cited as a hindrance, a report of the agriculture department in November 2025 points out that the cost of relief measures like setting up camps is much higher than the expense for the preventive measures. This strengthens the suspicion of the people over the vested interests involved.

"Conducting relief camps and supplying relief camps are obviously a lucrative affair for those involved in it. That could be the reason why the political leaderships are not keen on pressing for lasting solutions," says M V Antony, secretary of Save Kuttanad Forum.

The key hindrance in carrying out regulated pumping is the lack of power supply. Only temporary power connections at subsidised rates are provided during the time of cultivation. Hence, various government departments as well as local people have been constantly demanding the government to carry out regulated pumping under the disaster relief funds.

"The officials who are supposed to address these issues are leaving the place as soon as floods begin. Hence the local people alone are suffering," says Kuttanad resident Benny.

Karnataka weather today is mostly gloomy, as IMD has issued an Orange Alert and Yellow Alert for several districts across Karnataka as widespread rainfall activity is expected to continue over the next 24 hours.
The weather department has forecast heavy to very heavy rainfall which will come along with strong winds of 30-40 kmph, particularly across the coastal and Malnad regions.
IMD Issues Orange Alert for Karnataka Weather
An Orange Alert has been issued for Dakshina Kannada, Shivamogga, and Chikkamagaluru districts for August 7.
According to the IMD, these districts are expected to receive heavy to very heavy rainfall at some places. Strong winds with speeds of 30-40 kmph are also expected during the period.
Yellow Alert Issued for Multiple Karnataka Districts
The IMD has also issued a Yellow Alert for several districts like Uttara Kannada, Kodagu and Udupi where heavy rainfall between 64.5 mm and 115.4 mm intensity can be expected at some locations on August 7th
For August 8 the Yellow Alert has been extended to Dakshina Kannada, Udupi, Uttara Kannada, Shivamogga, Chikkamagaluru
Apart from the districts under Orange and Yellow Alerts some parts of Karnataka are also under radar including Ballari, Bengaluru Urban, Bengaluru Rural, Chamarajanagara, Chikkaballapura, Chitradurga, Davangere, Hassan, Kolar, Mandya, Mysuru, Ramanagara, Tumakuru, Vijayanagara
Coastal Karnataka Weather Forecast
According to IMD's 24-hour rainfall forecast, Coastal Karnataka will be experiencing active monsoon conditions in areas such as Dakshina Kannada, Udupi, Uttara Kannada, and Kodagu.
Bengaluru Weather Today
Bengaluru weather on Friday has been cloudy & gloomy so far, and the IMD has forecast light to moderate rainfall in several parts of the city. The rainy weather today can bring cooler temperatures, but also the possibility of temporary traffic congestion and waterlogging in low-lying areas is expected.
Safety Advisory During Heavy Rain In Karnataka
For people living in the heavy rain affected districts must avoid unnecessary travel during periods of heavy rainfall. One must stay away from rivers, streams, and flooded roads and be alert for landslides in hilly and ghat regions.
